title: Benefits
novel:
Ted and Robin were [[arguing|argue]] constantly as roommates. Every day brought a new [[conflict|conflict]] over dishes, TV volume, or bathroom schedules. The [[tension|tension]] was [[unbearable|unbearable]].

Then they discovered a [[solution|solution]]: whenever they argued, they would resolve it [[physically|physically]]. They became "friends with [[benefits|benefit]]." The arrangement [[worked|work]] — the fighting stopped, and the apartment was peaceful.

Barney was [[furious|furious]]. He had feelings for Robin and could not [[tolerate|tolerate]] the idea of Ted and Robin together. He tried to [[sabotage|sabotage]] their arrangement at every turn.

"This is a terrible idea," Barney [[warned|warn]]. "Someone will get [[hurt|hurt]]."

Marshall [[caught|catch]] Ted and Robin in a [[compromising|compromise]] position. He was [[shocked|shock]] and [[disgusted|disgust]]. "I can never [[unsee|unsee]] that," he said.

The arrangement eventually [[fell apart|fall apart]]. Ted and Robin realized that mixing friendship and [[intimacy|intimacy]] only [[complicated|complicate]] things. The [[boundaries|boundary]] were too [[blurry|blurry]].

"We can't keep doing this," Robin said.

"You're right," Ted [[agreed|agree]].

They went back to being just roommates. The arguments returned, but at least things were [[normal|normal]] again.

Barney felt [[relieved|relieve]] but also [[jealous|jealous]]. He watched Robin from afar, [[wondering|wonder]] if he would ever have the [[courage|courage]] to tell her how he felt.

solution.en: a way of solving a problem

physically.en: in a way related to the body

tolerate.en: to accept something you do not like

warn.en: to tell someone about a danger

unsee.en: to wish you could forget seeing something

boundary.en: a line that marks a limit

relieve.en: to make someone feel less worried

jealous.en: feeling angry because someone has what you want

courage.en: the ability to do something frightening
